_comment: The comparison table's data. `site/tools/build.py` renders it and nothing else
writes it, which is the same split `content/ideas.json` has: data here, markup there.
Rules this file is held to, and `build_compare()` enforces every one of them:
- every row carries a cell for every tool, so a blank is impossible rather than
- every cell names at least one source id, and every source id is defined below;
- every defined source is cited by at least one cell, so a link cannot rot into
- `v` is one of yes | partial | no | unclear, and `unclear` is the correct answer
whenever the sources checked did not settle it. Guessing on a public comparison
is how one gets taken apart.
`checked` is the date every URL below was read. It is printed on the page, because
several of these projects move weekly and a comparison with no date is a claim about

conductor.t: Proprietary. Free tier, then paid plans.

superset.t: Elastic License 2.0. Source-available, and its own site says not OSI-approved open source.

warp.t: The client is AGPL-3.0 with two MIT UI crates. The service around it is paid.

rows.label: Runs entirely on hardware you control

swemux.t: No server, no account, no relay. The project operates nothing.

herdr.t: A local binary. Remote means your own SSH or your own rented box.

tmux.t: A local process, and nothing else.

orca.t: A desktop app on your own subscriptions, with SSH to your own VPS.

conductor.t: Local workspaces on the free plan; Conductor Cloud is a paid tier.

superset.t: Local-first, and it states it never proxies model API calls.

warp.t: The terminal is local; Warp Drive, cloud agents, and conversation storage are account-backed.

swemux.t: The proving platform, and the only one with a packaged desktop application.

herdr.t: Stable-channel Windows binaries; ARM64 runs the x86_64 build under emulation.

tmux.t: OpenBSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, Linux, macOS, Solaris. Windows only inside WSL or Cygwin.

conductor.t: macOS only. Its own copy says 'on your Mac'.

superset.t: macOS primary, an experimental Linux AppImage, Windows not yet available.

swemux.t: The wheel installs and the CLI runs, proven in CI. No CI job on any host has ever started a daemon, so the daemon on macOS is unproven, and there is no desktop application for it.

conductor.t: The only platform it ships on.

swemux.t: A supervisor process separate from the daemon and the UI holds every terminal, so a daemon restart and a rebuild of the application itself leave the agents working. A reboot still ends the processes; the sessions stay readable afterwards.

herdr.t: Detach and reattach from any terminal or over SSH; its site states sessions survive restarts.

tmux.t: The server keeps sessions after every client detaches. Not across a reboot.

orca.t: Scrollback recovery after restart is documented; whether the process itself survives is not stated in the sources checked.

conductor.t: Not stated in the sources checked.

warp.t: Not stated for the local terminal in the sources checked.

swemux.t: Worktree creation and removal, plus a serialized land queue: reconcile with the trunk, run the verification command whose exact bytes you approved, then fast-forward only.

herdr.t: Not described in the sources checked.

tmux.t: Out of scope. tmux knows nothing about git.

orca.t: 'Every task runs in its own isolated git worktree.'

conductor.t: Each workspace is created as its own git worktree and branch.

superset.t: 'Each agent gets an isolated Git worktree and its own branch.'

warp.t: Not described in the sources checked.

swemux.t: Any CLI or shell runs unchanged, including one swe-mux has never heard of. The registry that adds status, transcripts, history, and account switching on top recognizes fewer of them than Orca or Herdr list.

herdr.t: '21 agents detected out of the box.'

tmux.t: None. It multiplexes terminals and does not read what is inside them.

orca.t: Names more than twenty CLI agents by hand, and states any CLI agent works.

conductor.t: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode.

superset.t: Names six and states any CLI-based coding agent works.

warp.t: Ships its own Agent CLI; other agents run inside it as ordinary terminal programs.

swemux.t: An installable web app reached over your own tailnet, with no relay and no swe-mux login.

herdr.t: No first-party client. Reachable from a phone by SSH into the host and attaching.

conductor.t: Announced as coming soon, not shipping on the date below.

superset.t: Not mentioned in the sources checked.

warp.t: Not mentioned in the sources checked.

rows.label: Voice control of the tool itself

swemux.t: Hands-free conversation: on-device wake words, dictation, spoken navigation and commands, and read-aloud.

herdr.t: Not described in the sources checked.

orca.t: Voice dictation with on-device models. Dictating into an agent, rather than driving the application.

conductor.t: Not mentioned in the sources checked.

superset.t: Not mentioned in the sources checked.

warp.t: Not mentioned in the sources checked.

rows.label: Evidence about a run that is not the agent's own transcript

swemux.t: Deterministic facts captured at the tool boundary - content hashes, parsed test outcomes, git tree hashes - and commit-level provenance separating who authored a change from who landed it. Off by default, per Project.

herdr.t: Semantic agent state forwarded by the agent integrations over its socket API. Status rather than an evidence record.

orca.t: No counterpart found in the sources checked.

conductor.t: No counterpart found in the sources checked.

superset.t: No counterpart found in the sources checked.

warp.t: No counterpart found in the sources checked.

rows.label: Deciding which agent to look at next

swemux.t: Ranked attention items with a hard daily interrupt budget, four a day by default, incident merging, and suppressed counts always shown rather than hidden.

herdr.t: A sidebar marking each agent working, blocked or idle. A view, not a budget.

orca.t: A fleet view with native notifications.

conductor.t: A dashboard of what the agents are doing.

superset.t: A workspace list. Its own roadmap names human review, not agent count, as the bottleneck.

warp.t: Not described in the sources checked.

swemux.t: None, and none planned. Your machine, or a machine you own.

herdr.t: A local binary. 'A box you rent' is still your box.

orca.t: SSH to your own VPS rather than a hosted runner.

conductor.t: Conductor Cloud, with cloud workspace hours, from the paid tier upward.

superset.t: Local-first, with no hosted execution in the sources checked.

warp.t: Warp Factories: cloud infrastructure for running fleets of coding agents.

swemux.t: A single-operator tool. No multi-tenancy, no role model, no audit subsystem, and none planned.

herdr.t: Not described in the sources checked.

tmux.t: Several people can attach to one session on a host they all have accounts on. Not a product feature so much as a consequence.

orca.t: Not described in the sources checked.

conductor.t: A Teams plan with live collaboration and admin controls, and SSO on Enterprise.

superset.t: Paid seats above the free tier.

warp.t: Business and Enterprise plans with collaboration features.
